title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #4

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How many cardinal points are there on a compass? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Six
   C. Eight
   D. Two

2. How many counties does Kenya have? (1 mark)
   A. 37
   B. 47
   C. 57
   D. 27

3. Which county borders Uganda? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Busia
   C. Nairobi
   D. Nyeri

4. Which is the highest mountain in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Mount Kenya
   B. Ngong Hills
   C. Aberdare Range
   D. Mount Elgon

5. Which of these is a problem of the rainy season? (1 mark)
   A. Very dry grass
   B. Flooding and muddy roads
   C. Shortage of rain
   D. Thick dust

6. In many parts of Kenya, when do the short rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. June to July
   B. October to December
   C. March to May
   D. January only

7. Which clothing is most suitable in the cold season? (1 mark)
   A. Sweaters and jackets
   B. Swimming costumes
   C. Light shorts only
   D. Sandals only

8. Which of these places is likely to be coldest in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The slopes of Mount Kenya
   B. A low dry plain
   C. A beach
   D. The coast

9. Why do tourists visit historic places? (1 mark)
   A. To plant maize
   B. To learn about the past and enjoy the sights
   C. To cut trees
   D. To buy soap

10. Why was Fort Jesus built? (1 mark)
   A. To guard the harbour
   B. To keep cattle
   C. To make sugar
   D. To grow food

11. Which of these is a good? (1 mark)
   A. Driving a matatu
   B. Teaching
   C. A pair of shoes
   D. Nursing

12. Why is population distribution useful to county planners? (1 mark)
   A. It helps them to move rivers
   B. It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
   C. It helps them to grow tea
   D. It helps them to change the weather

13. In traditional culture, what do we call a basket or clay pot made and used by people? (1 mark)
   A. A type of weather
   B. A kind of food
   C. An artefact
   D. A river

14. Which is a ceremony? (1 mark)
   A. A wedding
   B. A road
   C. A market
   D. A rainy day

15. Which food is made of maize and beans mixed together? (1 mark)
   A. Mahamri
   B. Pilau
   C. Chapati
   D. Githeri

16. What is a festival? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of house
   B. A quiet day
   C. A big celebration
   D. A river

17. How do economic activities help a county government? (1 mark)
   A. They cause drought
   B. Businesses pay taxes and fees
   C. They close clinics
   D. They stop roads

18. What is mining? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting hair
   B. Taking minerals from the ground
   C. Catching fish
   D. Growing maize

19. Which of these is an economic activity? (1 mark)
   A. Watching clouds
   B. Sleeping
   C. Singing at bedtime
   D. Fishing

20. What is one way factories can protect the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Burn tyres
   B. Throw waste into rivers
   C. Cut all trees
   D. Treat waste before releasing it

21. Why are sugar factories usually built near cane farms? (1 mark)
   A. Cane is hard to find
   B. Sugar cannot be sold
   C. Farmers do not like factories
   D. Cane is heavy and costly to carry far

22. What is a factory? (1 mark)
   A. A large building where goods are made with machines
   B. A market
   C. A school
   D. A hospital

23. What is a cost? (1 mark)
   A. Salary
   B. Money spent on the project
   C. Money received
   D. Profit

24. Wanjiru sold 10 tomatoes but recorded only 8. What should she do? (1 mark)
   A. Correct the record and tell the treasurer
   B. Hide the money
   C. Blame a friend
   D. Keep quiet

25. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. The price of a book
   B. All the money spent
   C. Money borrowed
   D. Money left after paying all costs

26. Which is not a good reason to choose a project? (1 mark)
   A. It is safe
   B. It is wanted
   C. It is dangerous but exciting
   D. We have the skills

27. Being good even when nobody is watching is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Boasting
   B. Integrity
   C. Fashion
   D. Punishment

28. What should you do if something online makes you feel scared? (1 mark)
   A. Keep it secret
   B. Tell a trusted adult
   C. Meet the stranger
   D. Reply angrily

29. What is a duty? (1 mark)
   A. Something you are expected to do
   B. Something you may not do
   C. A gift
   D. A game

30. What is a peace corner? (1 mark)
   A. A place to fight
   B. A shop
   C. A place to hide
   D. A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem

31. What is the first step in solving a conflict peacefully? (1 mark)
   A. Stop and calm down
   B. Hit
   C. Run away
   D. Shout

32. Whose fault is it if a child is abused? (1 mark)
   A. The teacher only
   B. The neighbour
   C. The abuser, never the child
   D. The child

33. What are tally marks used for? (1 mark)
   A. Counting votes
   B. Measuring rain
   C. Painting
   D. Cooking

34. How are members of the Children's Government chosen? (1 mark)
   A. By luck at a market
   B. By election
   C. By buying votes
   D. By force

35. What should a Children's Government NOT do? (1 mark)
   A. Organise clean-up days
   B. Welcome visitors
   C. Represent pupils
   D. Punish other pupils by itself

36. Who takes over when the president of the Children's Government is absent? (1 mark)
   A. The parent
   B. The cook
   C. The visitor
   D. The deputy president

37. Who leads a location and is appointed by the national government? (1 mark)
   A. Pastor
   B. Clan elder
   C. Village poet
   D. Chief

38. Which quality means not boasting or looking down on others? (1 mark)
   A. Greed
   B. Anger
   C. Pride
   D. Humility

39. What does MCA stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Mayor of Central Area
   B. Member of the County Assembly
   C. Minister of County Administration
   D. Master of County Affairs

40. What is a duty of an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. Command the army
   B. Issue passports
   C. Run national hospitals
   D. Represent the people of the ward in the assembly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain two ways of showing appreciation to people who help us. (2 marks)

42. Explain three ways in which a county can benefit when its officers know its size and location well. (3 marks)

43. Explain what may happen in a community with dishonest leaders. (3 marks)

44. Explain how you can stay calm when you feel very angry. (3 marks)

45. Explain the difference between the size of a county and its population. (3 marks)

46. State two things that a visitor can learn in a museum. (2 marks)

47. Name the two main parts of a county government and state what each does. (4 marks)

48. Give three reasons why historic built environments are important. (3 marks)

49. Describe how your class could showcase its school enterprise project. (5 marks)

50. Explain why many families live near towns and rivers. (3 marks)

51. Name three natural resources found in Kenya and say how each is used. (3 marks)

52. Explain why discipline is important in school. (3 marks)

53. Explain the meaning of profit and show how to find it. (3 marks)

54. Explain why a ballot should be secret. (2 marks)

55. A pupil stands facing east. Say what is behind the pupil, on the left and on the right. (3 marks)

56. Describe how you would show a river, a lake and a mountain on a map with a key. (3 marks)

57. What is meant by a densely populated area? (2 marks)

58. Explain why we say that the compass is useful in a county. (5 marks)

59. Name the three main kinds of historic built environments. (3 marks)

60. What does the Kiswahili word amani mean and why is it important in a school? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Four
   There are four cardinal points: north, east, south and west.

2. B — 47
   The Constitution of Kenya 2010 created 47 counties.

3. B — Busia
   Busia is on the border with Uganda.

4. A — Mount Kenya
   Mount Kenya is the highest mountain in Kenya.

5. B — Flooding and muddy roads
   Heavy rain can flood rivers and make roads muddy.

6. B — October to December
   The short rains usually come between October and December.

7. A — Sweaters and jackets
   Warm clothing keeps us comfortable when it is cold.

8. A — The slopes of Mount Kenya
   High places are colder than low places.

9. B — To learn about the past and enjoy the sights
   Tourism brings income to the local people.

10. A — To guard the harbour
   It was built as a stone fort to guard the harbour.

11. C — A pair of shoes
   Goods are things we can touch and use.

12. B — It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
   Services should reach people where they live.

13. C — An artefact
   Baskets and pots are artefacts.

14. A — A wedding
   A wedding is a special event with customs.

15. D — Githeri
   Githeri is maize and beans.

16. C — A big celebration
   Festivals are big celebrations with songs and dances.

17. B — Businesses pay taxes and fees
   Taxes and fees help pay for services.

18. B — Taking minerals from the ground
   Mining takes minerals such as soda ash or titanium from the earth.

19. D — Fishing
   Fishing produces food and income.

20. D — Treat waste before releasing it
   Treating waste avoids pollution.

21. D — Cane is heavy and costly to carry far
   Being near saves transport costs.

22. A — A large building where goods are made with machines
   Factories use machines to make goods.

23. B — Money spent on the project
   Costs are expenses.

24. A — Correct the record and tell the treasurer
   Records must be honest and complete.

25. D — Money left after paying all costs
   Profit = income - costs.

26. C — It is dangerous but exciting
   A project must be safe for children.

27. B — Integrity
   Integrity means doing right when unseen.

28. B — Tell a trusted adult
   A trusted adult can help.

29. A — Something you are expected to do
   A duty is a responsibility.

30. D — A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem
   A peace corner helps pupils settle problems.

31. A — Stop and calm down
   We must calm down before talking.

32. C — The abuser, never the child
   Abuse is never the child's fault.

33. A — Counting votes
   Tally marks help count votes.

34. B — By election
   Pupils vote for their leaders.

35. D — Punish other pupils by itself
   Only teachers decide on discipline.

36. D — The deputy president
   The deputy helps and takes over.

37. D — Chief
   A chief leads a location.

38. D — Humility
   Humble leaders are modest.

39. B — Member of the County Assembly
   MCA is a Member of the County Assembly.

40. D — Represent the people of the ward in the assembly
   MCAs represent their wards.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Say thank you and treat their work with respect. Accept helping them in return.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: They can plan roads and health centres to reach people. They can share resources with neighbours. They can plan journeys and services better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Resources are wasted, people lose trust, and people quarrel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk away, take slow deep breaths, and count to ten before speaking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Size is the area of land a county covers. Population is the number of people who live there. A big county can have few people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for size, 1 mark for population, 1 mark for the difference or example.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: How people lived long ago and which tools they used. Accept learning about animals, plants and cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: The county executive runs the county and carries out laws. The county assembly makes county laws and checks the executive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part and 1 mark for each job.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: They teach us history, they give us identity and pride, and they bring tourists and income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Set up a stall with the goods, display a poster, show records of costs and income, explain each team member's role, and let visitors ask questions and give feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Towns have jobs, schools and shops. Rivers give water for drinking and farming. These things make life easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for towns, 1 mark for rivers, 1 mark for making life easier.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is used for drinking and farming. Land is used for farming and grazing. Minerals such as soda ash are used in factories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each resource with a use.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the school orderly, it helps everyone learn, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Profit is the money left after all costs are paid. Profit = income - costs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for formula, 1 mark for correct example.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: So that nobody can force or influence how a person votes, so the choice is free.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind is west. On the left is north. On the right is south.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wavy blue line for a river, a blue patch for a lake and a brown triangle or brown shading for a mountain, with a key that explains them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct symbol described, up to 3.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: An area where many people live close together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many people, 1 mark for close together.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: It helps us to find our way. It helps mapmakers to draw maps. It helps us to describe where places are. It helps drivers and sailors to travel. It helps us to plan journeys.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point, up to 5.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Museums, monuments and cultural centres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct kind.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Amani means peace. It is important because pupils feel safe and can learn well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 mark for the reason.
